prs.title: feat(oxfmt)!: format `parser:html` files by `oxc_formatter_htmlish`
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Fixes #28263

- Before this PR: `.html` and also html-in-{js,md,etc} are formatted by Prettier.
  - Because of that, we had to run JS, which became an overhead.
- After this PR: All of them are formatted natively by `oxc_formatter_htmlish`.
  - No overhead.

At the same time, since we are fixing Prettier bugs and inconsistent behavior, please refer to DIVERGENCES.md for the differences.

feat(track_memory_allocs): add allocation tracking for linter rules
prs.author: camchenry
prs.body:
As an alternative to https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/27477, this requires minimal changes in the linter in order to add allocation tracking for individual rules. We run each rule individually and then compare the diff in heap size before and after as well as the number of system and arena allocations.

Additionally, this runs as a local-only opt-in feature so that we don't check this in CI automatically, since linter allocations are likely quite noisy.

refactor(lexer): compile `carve` separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `carve`, `carve_js` and `carve_jsx`, and pass `cpu` to `carve` from `lex_raw_impl`. `carve_js` and `carve_jsx` don't use `cpu` yet.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): pass `cpu` to `carve`'s string, template and slash helpers
refactor(lexer): compile comment lexing separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

`lex_line_comment`, `lex_block_comment`, `html_open_comment_at` and `html_close_comment_at` take `cpu`. They're `#[inline(always)]`, so they stay that way. Apply `cpu_versions!` to the other functions in `carve/comments.rs` that they call, keeping their inline attributes. None of these functions use `cpu` for SIMD yet.

The cold `lex_html_open_comment` and `lex_html_close_comment` are compiled only once, so they pass `BASELINE`. `BASELINE` is now used outside tests, so remove the `expect(unused_imports)` on its re-exports.

This changes codegen slightly. `classify` now has 2 copies, so `str::trim_matches` (from `.trim()` in `is_property_key_annotation`) is no longer inlined into it. `html_close_at_line_start` differs slightly on all platforms. On aarch64, `carve` and `carve_jsx` lay out the code that pushes comments a little differently. No other functions are affected, apart from register allocation in the generic copy of `carve` on x86_64.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile JSX angle bracket disambiguation separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `jsx_over_type_params` and `ts_angle_verdict`, keeping their `#[inline]` attributes. `carve_jsx` passes `cpu` to `jsx_over_type_params`, which passes it on to `ts_angle_verdict`. `ts_angle_verdict` doesn't use `cpu` yet.

This changes codegen on x86_64 only. `jsx_over_type_params` is inlined into `carve_jsx` again, as it was before step B1. No change on aarch64.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile JSX name and trivia helpers separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

`jsx_skip_trivia_fast` takes `cpu`. It's `#[inline(always)]`, so it stays that way. Apply `cpu_versions!` to the other functions in `carve/jsx/names.rs` which `carve_jsx` and `ts_angle_verdict` call, apart from the `#[inline(always)]` `is_jsx_name_byte`, which calls nothing that needs a CPU type. They keep their inline attributes. `is_jsx_name_byte_at`, `jsx_skip_trivia` and `jsx_name_end` don't use `cpu` yet.

This changes codegen slightly. On x86_64, `jsx_names_equal_fast` is inlined into `carve_jsx` again, as it was before step B1. On aarch64, `carve_jsx` makes 12 calls to `classify` instead of 16, and is about 200 instructions shorter. `jsx_name_next` changes trivially on all platforms.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `find_line_terminator` separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `find_line_terminator`, keeping its `#[inline]` attribute. It doesn't use `cpu` yet. `carve_js`, `carve_jsx` and `jsx_skip_trivia` pass it `cpu`. The cold `lex_html_open_comment` and `lex_html_close_comment` are compiled only once, so they pass `BASELINE`.

No change to codegen.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Lanes` string methods separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Lanes::push_string`, `push_template`, `push_string_raw` and `push_regex_flags`, keeping their `#[inline]` attributes. They don't use `cpu` yet. `lex_string`, `lex_template_segment`, `lex_regex` and `carve_jsx` pass them `cpu`. A test passes `BASELINE`.

This changes codegen. On aarch64, `push_string` and `push_template` are no longer inlined into `carve` and `carve_jsx`. Instead, `cook` is inlined into them, so the number of calls per string or template is unchanged. On x86_64, register allocation changes in `carve` and `carve_jsx`.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Lanes` atom and number methods separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Lanes::push_atom` and `push_number`, keeping their `#[inline]` attributes. They don't use `cpu` yet.

`compress`'s `emit_value` takes `cpu`. It's `#[inline(always)]`, so it stays that way. `lanes_post_avx2` passes it its `Avx2`. `lanes_post_generic` now needs a CPU type too, so it takes `cpu` and gets `cpu_versions!`. `lanes_post` passes it the CPU type from its `Neon` and `Generic` arms.

This changes inlining in `compress`. On x86_64, `push_number` is now inlined into `compress`, and `parse_number` is no longer inlined into `push_number`. `push_atom` is no longer inlined into `compress`. On aarch64, `push_atom` is no longer inlined into `compress`. Instead, `cook` is inlined into `push_atom`.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Lanes` cooking separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Lanes::cook`, `cook_short_dispatch`, `cook_decode`, `push_cp` and `emit_oct`, keeping their inline attributes. `push_cp` and `emit_oct` don't use `cpu` yet. `push_string`, `push_template` and `push_atom` pass `cpu` to `cook`. Tests pass `BASELINE`.

Replace the 2 cfg'd versions of `cook_short` with an `#[inline(always)]` dispatcher which uses `cpu_select!`. `cook_short_avx2` gets `#[target_feature]` and takes `cpu: Avx2`, which it passes to `cook_decode`. It no longer needs `unsafe` blocks around the intrinsics which don't access memory. `cook_short_generic` gets `cpu_versions!`, because it passes `cpu` to `cook_decode`.

This changes inlining on x86_64, as step B7 did on aarch64. `cook` is now inlined into `push_string`, `push_template` and `push_atom`, which are no longer inlined into `carve` and `carve_jsx`. So the number of calls per string or template is unchanged. On aarch64, `cook_decode::<false, true>` is 52 instructions longer, with the same calls.

On x86_64, the AVX2 versions of `push_string`, `push_template` and `push_atom` now use `cook_short_avx2`. In builds with AVX2 flags, their generic versions use `cook_short_generic`, as intended for step D5.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile number parsing separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `parse_number`, `radix_digit` and `validate_number`, keeping their inline attributes. `parse_number` and `radix_digit` don't use `cpu` yet. `Lanes::push_number` passes `cpu` to `parse_number` and `validate_number`.

This changes inlining on x86_64, undoing step B8's change to `push_number`. `parse_number` is inlined into `push_number` again, and `push_number` is no longer inlined into `compress`, as before step B8. `push_number` is now the same as before step B1. On aarch64, branches in `push_number` change slightly.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile scalar scanners separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `scan_quoted`, `scan_regex`, `scan_tmpl_text`, `scan_ident_esc`, `scan_number` and `scan_fraction_exponent`, keeping their `#[inline]` attributes. Only `scan_number` uses `cpu` so far, to pass it to `scan_fraction_exponent`.

`lex_string`, `lex_template_segment`, `lex_regex` and `coalesce`'s `glue_number` pass `cpu` to them. `misc_pre_impl` takes `cpu` from `misc_pre`, to pass to `scan_ident_esc`. It's `#[inline(always)]`, so it stays that way.

This changes codegen. On x86_64, `scan_number` and `scan_fraction_exponent` are now inlined into `coalesce`, as they already were on aarch64. Before, each was called from both copies of `coalesce`. Register allocation and branch layout change slightly in `carve`, `carve_jsx` and `scan_regex`, on all platforms.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): `#[inline(always)]` on `unicode_ws_len_at_unchecked`
refactor(lexer): compile operator position check separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `not_operator_position`, `ends_decl` and `paren_close_is_regex`. `lex_slash` and `carve_jsx` pass `cpu` to `not_operator_position`, which passes it on to the other two. `ends_decl` and `paren_close_is_regex` don't use `cpu` yet.

No change to codegen, apart from the new AVX2 versions in builds without AVX2 flags.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `jsx_over_generic` separately for each CPU feature set

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `>` run splitting separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `gt_run_split`, `run_shortcut`, `list_in_any_context`, `type_reference_head` and `return_type_colon`, keeping their inline attributes. `coalesce` and `glue_number` pass `cpu` to `gt_run_split`, which passes it down the chain. `return_type_colon` doesn't use `cpu` yet.

No change to codegen, apart from the new AVX2 versions in builds without AVX2 flags.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `DisambiguateState` methods separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `DisambiguateState::begin` and `restart`. `lex_raw_impl` passes `cpu` to `begin`, and `coalesce` passes it to `restart`. Neither uses `cpu` yet.

This changes inlining on x86_64. `begin` was called out of line from both copies of `lex_raw_impl`. Now each copy inlines its own `begin`, including the small `Walks::restart`, and calls `Brackets::begin` out of line instead. This is setup code which runs once per lex. No change on aarch64.

prs.title: ci(lexer): remove `oxc_lexer` benchmark
refactor(lexer): compile type argument checks separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `gt_follower`, `type_list_legal`, `keyword_type`, `type_args_at` and `list_is_type_args`, keeping their inline attributes. `list_in_any_context` passes `cpu` to `type_args_at`. `gt_follower` and `keyword_type` don't use `cpu` yet.

Level 3 is compiled only once, so its two callers, `Walk::less_than` and `Walk::type_word`, use `BASELINE`.

This changes inlining on x86_64. The AVX2 version of `type_args_at` now has only one caller, so it's inlined into the AVX2 version of `gt_run_split`, which grows from about 950 instructions to about 3,000. Its generic version is still called out of line, from Level 3 and from the generic version of `gt_run_split`. On aarch64, register allocation changes in `type_args_at`.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile forward bracket scans separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `lt_run_split`, `arrow_after_params`, `skip_trivia_fwd`, `list_closer`, `group_closer`, `past_raw`, `resolve_lists`, `kill`, `resolve_groups`, `skip_raw_literal`, `past_raw_string` and `raw_template_end` in `type_context/bytes.rs`, keeping their inline attributes. `skip_trivia_nl` takes `cpu`. It's `#[inline(always)]`, so it stays that way. `kill`, `past_raw_string` and `skip_trivia_nl` don't use `cpu` yet.

`coalesce`, `jsx_over_generic`, `gt_follower`, `type_list_legal` and `type_args_at` pass `cpu` to them. Level 3 is compiled only once, so `Walk::step_op` uses `BASELINE` for `lt_run_split`.

This changes codegen slightly. Register allocation changes in the cold `raw_template_end` on all platforms, and operand order in `skip_raw_literal` on aarch64.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Tokens` methods separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Tokens::base_kind`, `word_kw`, `ident_kw`, `next_start`, `next_sig`, `peek`, `prev_sig`, `prev_token`, `property_name`, `member_dot`, `numeric_dot`, `run_len`, `line_break_between`, `ident_is` and `match_delim_back`, keeping their inline attributes. Their callers in Levels 1 and 2 pass their `cpu`. `ends_decl`, `paren_close_is_regex` and `return_type_colon` now use theirs.

Level 3 is compiled only once, so the Level 3 functions which call these methods use `BASELINE`. So do `Tokens::template_head` and `Prev::is_member_dot`, which only Level 3 calls.

This changes inlining. `Tokens::ident_kw` and `Tokens::ident_is` are now called out of line from `prev_token`, `gt_run_split`, `type_args_at` and Level 3. In Level 3, `Walk::step` no longer inlines `Tokens::next_start`, `Walk::asi`, `Walk::end_region_for` or `Walk::continues_after_type_break`, so it shrinks from about 1,950 instructions to about 1,140. `not_operator_position` is unchanged on aarch64, and changes slightly on x86_64.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile backward token walking separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to the free `prev_sig`, `Brackets::begin`, `Brackets::word`, `bracket_word`, `match_delim_back`, `delim_memo_opener`, `delim_slot` and `ident_is` in `common/walk.rs`, keeping their inline attributes. `Tokens::prev_sig`, `Tokens::ident_is`, `Tokens::match_delim_back`, `DisambiguateState::begin` and `carve_jsx` pass them `cpu`. `prev_sig`, `Brackets::begin`, `bracket_word`, `delim_slot` and `ident_is` don't use `cpu` yet.

This changes inlining on x86_64 only. `Brackets::begin` is inlined into each copy of `lex_raw_impl` again, which step C4 had undone. `Tokens::match_delim_back` is called out of line again, with `match_delim_back` inlined into it, as before step C7. No change on aarch64.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Closers` methods separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Resolved::closer`, `Closers::clear`, `Closers::get`, `Closers::set` and `Closers::set_args`, keeping their inline attributes. Their callers pass `cpu`. `DisambiguateState::restart` and `kill` now use theirs. None of these methods use `cpu` yet.

This changes inlining on x86_64. Each copy of `resolve_lists` and `resolve_groups` now inlines `Closers::set`, which was called out of line. They call the standard library's `HashMap::insert` out of line instead. These are cold paths, which run only for forward scans past their byte cap. On aarch64, `arrow_after_params` and `list_closer` change trivially.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `kw_match_at` separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `kw_match_at`, keeping its `#[inline]` attribute. It doesn't use `cpu` yet. `Tokens::word_kw`, `gt_follower` and `type_list_legal` pass it `cpu`. Tests pass `BASELINE`.

No change to codegen, apart from the new AVX2 version in builds without AVX2 flags.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile byte scans in `bytes.rs` separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `unicode_ws_len_at`, `line_terminator_after`, `line_break_in` and `block_comment_end`, keeping their inline attributes. `line_break_in` passes `cpu` to `line_terminator_after`. The others don't use `cpu` yet. Their callers pass `cpu`, and `Tokens::line_break_between`, `ident_is` and `skip_trivia_nl` now use theirs.

This changes inlining slightly. `line_terminator_after` is now inlined into `line_break_in`, which is called out of line instead. No other changes, apart from the new AVX2 versions in builds without AVX2 flags.

prs.title: refactor(lexer): compile `Lexer::ensure` separately for each CPU feature set
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Part of effort to move to runtime CPU feature detection.

Apply `cpu_versions!` to `Lexer::ensure`. It doesn't use `cpu` yet. `lex_raw_impl` passes `cpu`. `Lexer::lex` also calls it, outside the runtime switch, so it uses `BASELINE`, which adds no runtime dispatch.

Codegen: aarch64 is unchanged, with `ensure` out of line as before. On x86_64, the AVX2 copy of `ensure` has only one caller, so it's now inlined into the AVX2 copy of `lex_raw_impl`, which grows by about 410 instructions. It runs once per lex. `Lexer::lex` and the generic copy of `lex_raw_impl` call the generic copy out of line, as before. The generic code's instruction count is unchanged.
